title: Full Roos realization of completed integral tensor
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and schemes in a universe $u$ [def-pc-scheme]. For a scheme $W$, use its small pro-etale ringed sequence site $\mathbf N\times W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, whose index $n\geq0$ means $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^{n+1})_W$, with actual quotient ring maps; put $A_W=\lim_nB_{W,n}$ and let $\mathscr S_W$ be its category of module sheaves, equivalently strict quotient-semilinear systems [def-coef-ringed-sequence-site]. Write $e_{W,n}$ for exact evaluation, $\operatorname{Res}_{W,n}$ for restriction along $A_W\to B_{W,n}$ and $U_W:\mathscr S_W\to\operatorname{Tow}(\operatorname{Mod}(A_W))$ for their simultaneous exact scalar restriction. Use ordinary unbounded integer-indexed cochain and derived categories, with localization $q_W$ for $A_W$-modules, $q^s_W$ for sequence modules and $q^t_W$ for towers [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$, with $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\circ D(U_W)$, and the specified derived tensor and cochain tensor models on the sequence site [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. A good integral complex is K-flat with flat terms; K-flat means that its direct-sum total tensor with every acyclic module complex is acyclic [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. All comparisons below use the actual chosen adjunctions, not arbitrary isomorphisms between their objects. No boundedness, constructibility, completeness of inputs, or invertibility of $\ell$ on the schemes is assumed. Write $L^0_W=\lim\circ U_W$ and $r_W=\operatorname{leftAdjoint}(L^0_W)$ for ordinary coherent reduction, equipped with its specified adjunction $r_W\dashv L^0_W$ and unit $\eta^0_W$; concretely its components are quotient extension $B_{W,n}\otimes_{A_W}M$ and its transitions are induced by the actual quotient maps. A superscript $c$ means termwise application to cochain complexes. For a coherent complex $C$, let $\lambda_C:q_W((L^0_W)^c C)\to\mathcal L_W(q^s_WC)$ be the canonical right-derived limit unit, with the exact-restriction/localization factorization inserted (the map named pullbackTensorLimitUnit). For a complex $T$ of strict $A_W$-module towers, let $J_W(T)$ denote reordering to a tower of complexes, and put $H_W(T)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_nJ_W(T)_n\to\prod_nJ_W(T)_n)[-1]$, where $s((x_n))=(t_nx_{n+1})$ uses the actual transitions [def-sf-strict-roos-functor]. Write $H_W$ also for the resulting cochain functor. The map $j_I:(\lim)^c I\to H_W(I)$ is the mapping-cocone lift whose unshifted product component is the family of ordinary limit projections and whose shifted product component is zero. This specifies the map, not merely its finite projections. Let $m_W:\mathcal R_Wq_W|_{\mathrm{good}}\xrightarrow{\sim}q^s_Wr_W^c|_{\mathrm{good}}$ be the derived reduction model fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism whose transpose under the fixed derived adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ is, for every good $P$, exactly $\lambda_{r_W^cP}\circ q_W((\eta^0_W)^c_P)$. Let $\rho_W:(R\lim)q^t_W\xrightarrow{\sim}q_WH_W$ be the total-limit/Roos model fixed in [def-pur-completed-pullback-tower-core]: the unique natural isomorphism on all complexes of strict $A_W$-module towers whose component at every K-injective tower complex $I$ is $q_W(j_I)\circ\operatorname{rightDerivedFunctorObjQIso}(\lim,I).\mathrm{hom}$. Use the strict tensor tower comparison $d$ [lem-pur-coherent-tensor-tower], and K-flatness of $r_W^cP$ for good $P$ [lem-pur-coherent-reduction-kflat]. Write $\tau_W(P',Q'):\operatorname{Tot}_s(P',Q')$ localized $\xrightarrow{\sim}(q^s_WP')\otimes_s^L(q^s_WQ')$ for exactly the fixed coherent K-flat tensor model. Define
$$T_W^{\mathrm{ref}}(K,L)=\mathcal L_W(\mathcal R_WK\otimes_s^L\mathcal R_WL).$$
For good $P,Q$, define $\nu_{W,P,Q}:T_W^{\mathrm{ref}}(q_WP,q_WQ)\xrightarrow{\sim}q_WH_W(B_\otimes^0(P,Q))$ by applying $\mathcal L_W$ to $m_P\otimes_s^Lm_Q$, then to $\tau_W(r_W^cP,r_W^cQ)^{-1}$, then inserting exact-restriction factorization and $\rho_W$, and then $q_WH_W(d_{P,Q})$. Let $\widehat\otimes_W$ and $\epsilon^\otimes_{P,Q}:q_WP\widehat\otimes_Wq_WQ\xrightarrow{\sim}q_WH_W(B_\otimes^0(P,Q))$ be the actual completed tensor and its fixed full strict-model comparison [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. There exists a unique natural isomorphism $\beta_W:\widehat\otimes_W\xrightarrow{\sim}T_W^{\mathrm{ref}}$ satisfying
$$\beta_{W,(q_WP,q_WQ)}=\nu_{W,P,Q}^{-1}\circ\epsilon^\otimes_{P,Q}\qquad\text{for every good }P,Q.$$
This is pullbackTensorIntegralTensorModel_existsUnique; the equation is the expanded pullbackTensorIntegralTensorNormalization predicate, with the entire Roos chain model retained.

proof.text: Use the constructed natural coherent tensor-level comparison def-pur-natural-coherent-tensor-level. Its component at (P,Q) is definitionally the prescribed tensor-tower level isomorphism. Combine this component equation with the chosen tower normalization, then apply its naturality and tower extensionality. This proves naturality of the chosen strict tensor-tower isomorphism without unfolding the total-tensor construction in the main proof.

Apply the real constructor def-pur-coherent-tensor-roos-comparison to the proved K-flat preservation of ordinary reduction on good complexes and the natural strict tensor-tower comparison of step 1. Its component theorem identifies the resulting natural isomorphism with the entire prescribed pullbackTensorReferenceTensorModel(P,Q), including exact restriction, the full Roos differential and both cone coordinates.

Apply normalizedDescentComponents_existsUnique to the product good localization, the functor, comparison and universal property of integralCompletedTensorDescent, and the natural model comparison of the preceding step. The resulting natural isomorphism has the prescribed equation on every good pair. Replace each component of the natural model comparison by its definitionally equal recorded model component. This is exactly pullbackTensorIntegralTensorNormalization; the uniqueness clause of the same descent theorem proves uniqueness for this complete normalization.
